<ConnectorActions client:visible />

Connect a service once (usually an OAuth consent screen) and credentials are stored per tenant, available to every agent in the workspace. Per-tool limits on a [budget](/docs/build/budgets/) are enforced on workflow tool and connector nodes only.

## Available connectors (18)

Counted from the executor's dispatch table ([`connector_executor.go`](repo:/blob/master/services/control-plane/internal/handlers/connector_executor.go#L349-L383)).

### Communication

- **Slack** (`slack`): list channels and users, post messages, reply in threads; OAuth or bot token
- **Discord** (`discord`): list guilds, send messages; bot token or OAuth
- **Telegram** (`telegram`): send messages, fetch updates; bot token
- **Twilio** (`twilio`): send SMS, list messages, place calls, add conference participants; Account SID + Auth Token + phone number (or Messaging Service SID)

### Email and calendar

- **Gmail** (`gmail`): list, search and send mail; Google OAuth or email + app password
- **Google Calendar** (`google-calendar`): list and create events; Google OAuth

### Docs and storage

- **Google Drive** (`google-drive`): list files; Google OAuth
- **Google Sheets** (`google-sheets`): get a spreadsheet, get cell values; Google OAuth
- **Notion** (`notion`): search, list databases; OAuth or integration token

### Dev tools

- **GitHub** (`github`): list repos, list and get PRs, list and get issues, create issues, comment on PRs; OAuth or personal access token
- **Linear** (`linear`): list and create issues; API key or OAuth
- **Jira** (`jira`): list and create issues; email + API token + domain, or OAuth
- **Sentry** (`sentry`): list and get issues; auth token
- **PagerDuty** (`pagerduty`): list and get incidents, create and update incidents, add notes; REST API key. No dashboard card yet; install over the API (see [Newer actions](#newer-actions))
- **Vercel** (`vercel`): list projects and deployments; access token

### CRM and sales

- **HubSpot** (`hubspot`): list contacts and deals; API key or OAuth
- **Salesforce** (`salesforce`): run SOQL queries; access token + instance URL (OAuth supported)

### Commerce

- **Stripe** (`stripe`): list charges and customers; secret key or OAuth

<Aside>
**Web search** is a built-in tool, not a connector (sessions enable it with the `webSearch` flag). **Adding a connector** is a code change today: a new case in `connector_executor.go`. There is no plug-in interface yet.
</Aside>

## Newer actions

These actions run through `POST /v1/connectors/{id}/execute?action=<action>` with a JSON body of params (the connector must be installed and connected first). A successful call returns `{"connector", "action", "data"}`; a failed vendor call returns 502 with `{"error", "connector", "action"}`; an uninstalled connector returns 404.

Required params are marked **(required)**.

| Connector / action | Params | Credential (config field) | Class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `slack` / `reply_thread` | `channel` **(required)**, `text` **(required)**, `thread_ts` **(required)** | OAuth, or `botToken` | write |
| `github` / `comment_pr` | `owner` **(required)**, `repo` **(required)**, `number` **(required)**, `body` **(required)** | OAuth, or `personalAccessToken` | write |
| `sentry` / `get_issue` | `organization` **(required)**, `issue_id` **(required)** | `authToken` | read-only |
| `google-calendar` / `create_event` | `summary` **(required)**, `start` **(required)**, `end` **(required)** (RFC3339); optional `calendarId` (default `primary`), `timeZone`, `description`, `location`, `attendees` (array of emails) | Google OAuth | write |
| `pagerduty` / `list_incidents` | optional `status` (`triggered`, `acknowledged`, `resolved`), `limit` (default 25) | `apiKey` (REST API key) | read-only |
| `pagerduty` / `get_incident` | `incident_id` **(required)** | `apiKey` | read-only |
| `pagerduty` / `create_incident` | `title` **(required)**, `service_id` **(required)**, `from` **(required)** (acting user's email); optional `details` | `apiKey` | write |
| `pagerduty` / `update_incident` | `incident_id` **(required)**, `from` **(required)**, `status` **(required)** (`acknowledged` or `resolved`) | `apiKey` | write |
| `pagerduty` / `add_note` | `incident_id` **(required)**, `content` **(required)**, `from` **(required)** | `apiKey` | write |

Slack `post_message` also accepts an optional `thread_ts`; `reply_thread` is the same call with `thread_ts` required. "Read-only" is the allowlist in `connector_safety.go`; anything not on it, including every action on an unknown connector, is treated as side-effecting.

PagerDuty has no dashboard card yet. Install it over the API, then call it. Agents get `list_incidents` and `get_incident` as tools; `create_incident`, `update_incident` and `add_note` are REST-only (and usable from workflow connector nodes).

```bash
# install PagerDuty (config.apiKey = a REST API key)
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/connectors/install \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"connectorId": "pagerduty", "displayName": "PagerDuty", "config": {"apiKey": "..."}}'

# read an incident
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/connectors/pagerduty/execute?action=get_incident" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"incident_id": "PABC123"}'

# acknowledge it (write; "from" is required by PagerDuty)
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/connectors/pagerduty/execute?action=update_incident" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"incident_id": "PABC123", "from": "oncall@example.com", "status": "acknowledged"}'

# reply in a Slack thread
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/connectors/slack/execute?action=reply_thread" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel": "C0123", "thread_ts": "1700000000.000100", "text": "On it."}'
```

## Recorded test mode

Run connector actions without a real SaaS account by pointing a vendor at a local fixture server. This is dev and test only.

**1. Start the fixture server** from `services/control-plane`. It listens on loopback and serves recorded responses for Slack, GitHub, Sentry, PagerDuty and Google Calendar:

```bash
go run ./cmd/connector-replay            # 127.0.0.1:9191
go run ./cmd/connector-replay -addr 127.0.0.1:9292
```

**2. Point the control plane at it** before starting it (`PAL_ENV` must not be prod, production or staging):

```bash
export PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_SLACK=http://127.0.0.1:9191
export PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_GITHUB=http://127.0.0.1:9191
export PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_SENTRY=http://127.0.0.1:9191
export PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_GOOGLE=http://127.0.0.1:9191
export PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_PAGERDUTY=http://127.0.0.1:9191
make run-api
```

**3. Check it worked**: install a connector with any non-empty token, execute an action, then read what the server saw:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9191/__requests
```

Each recorded call has `method`, `path`, `query`, `header`, `body`, `hasAuth`, `matched` and `status`. The `Authorization` header is never stored, only whether it was set.

### Override variables

| Variable | Vendor host replaced | Connectors affected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_SLACK` | `slack.com` | Slack |
| `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_GITHUB` | `api.github.com` | GitHub |
| `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_SENTRY` | `sentry.io` | Sentry |
| `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_GOOGLE` | `www.googleapis.com` | Google Calendar, Google Drive |
| `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_PAGERDUTY` | `api.pagerduty.com` | PagerDuty |

The value must be an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host. Only scheme and host are replaced; the vendor path is kept, so the fixture server serves real paths such as `/api/chat.postMessage`. An unmatched request gets 404:

```json
{"error": "no recorded fixture for METHOD PATH"}
```

Fixtures are exact method + path matches in `internal/connectorreplay/fixtures.json` (embedded in the binary): Slack `conversations.list` and `chat.postMessage`; GitHub `acme/api` pulls list, PR 42, and a comment on 42; Sentry org `acme` issues list and issue `1001`; PagerDuty incidents list, get `PABC123`, create, update; Google Calendar `primary` events list and insert. Use those owner, repo, org and ids in your test params.

### Refused in production

A bearer token must never be sent to an arbitrary host, so overrides are blocked twice:

- **Startup:** with `PAL_ENV` set to `prod`, `production` or `staging`, the control plane exits if any override variable is set: `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_X set in production — connector base-URL overrides are test-only and would redirect tenant credentials to another host; unset them` (names of every variable set are listed). In any environment a malformed value is also fatal: `PAL_CONNECTOR_BASEURL_X is malformed: must be an absolute http(s) URL, got "..."`.
- **Request time:** the outbound transport ignores overrides whenever the environment is prod, even if one slipped in.

## Setting up a connector

### OAuth-based connectors

Most connectors support OAuth (Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Sheets, Slack, GitHub, Discord, Notion, Linear, Jira, HubSpot, Stripe, Salesforce) when the deployment has OAuth client credentials configured. In **Integrations** (`/connectors`), click the provider button (for example **Sign in with Google** or **Add to Slack**), authorize on the consent screen, and you land back with the connector installed.

<Aside type="tip">
Revoke access any time by uninstalling the connector (`DELETE /v1/connectors/{id}`).
</Aside>

### API key-based connectors

Telegram, Twilio, Sentry, PagerDuty and Vercel take a key or token. In **Integrations**, choose the manual option (for example **Enter bot token**) and fill in the credentials; they are tested before the connector shows as connected. Credentials are encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) when `PAL_CREDENTIAL_KEY` is set; without it they are plaintext, so set it outside dev.

<Aside type="caution">
Credentials never appear in logs, traces or run state. Connector actions run in the control plane, which resolves the credential at call time.
</Aside>

## Which agents can use a connector

Connectors are installed per workspace, not per agent: once connected, every agent in the workspace can call it. To limit blast radius, use [budgets](/docs/build/budgets/) `toolLimits` (workflow nodes only), the approval and confidence gates, or a separate workspace. The agent page's Connectors card is a read-only list linking to `/connectors`.

## How agents use connectors

Assigned connectors reach the LLM as tools; it decides when to call them. You can also call an action directly over REST:

```bash
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/connectors/gmail/execute?action=search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAL_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "from:boss@company.com subject:urgent"}'
```

PAL Runtime keeps an explicit allowlist of read-only actions (for example `list_*`, `get_*`, `search`, `query` on the built-in connectors); every other action, including any on an unknown connector, counts as side-effecting. Agents receive a curated subset of actions as tools (for example `github__list_prs`, `slack__post_message`, `gmail__search`); the full list above is always callable over REST and from workflow connector nodes. Install needs `connectors:write`; `execute` needs `runs:execute`. In the workflow engine, [confidence gating](/docs/pal/human-in-the-loop/) (off by default) can route side-effecting steps to a human first.

## Connector permissions

OAuth scopes come from `oauth_providers.go`:

- **Gmail**: `gmail.modify` (read, send, label; no permanent delete)
- **GitHub**: `repo`, `read:user`
- **Slack**: `channels:read`, `chat:write`, `users:read`

<Aside type="tip">
If a connector is missing or uninstalled, the action returns a missing-credentials error naming the connector.
</Aside>
